strings.name: Robert B. Wilson
strings.summary: Robert B. Wilson studies strategic interaction under asymmetric information, auctions and pricing. With David Kreps he developed sequential equilibrium, and he contributed to spectrum-auction and electricity-market design. In 2020 he shared the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences with Paul Milgrom.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Coauthors are credited; preprints, journal publication, future recall and completed service are distinguished. Theory is not presented as a guarantee of market performance.
strings.influence.rationale: Studies games with incomplete information and auction mechanisms, influencing electricity markets and spectrum allocation.
strings.facts.f1.label: Degrees
strings.facts.f1.value: Harvard: AB in 1959, MBA in 1961 and DBA in 1963; the doctorate is in business administration.
strings.facts.f2.label: Academic status
strings.facts.f2.value: Joined Stanford in 1964 and became emeritus in 2004. A 2026 notice lists a recall for April–June 2027.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Common values and the winner’s curse
strings.highlights.h1.text: Examines cautious bidding when common values are uncertain; this does not mean every winner loses money.
strings.highlights.h2.title: From game theory to market design
strings.highlights.h2.text: With collaborators, studies sequential equilibrium, nonlinear pricing and auction rules, connecting theory with spectrum and electricity markets.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Stanford announces future recall
strings.timeline.t1.text: The notice lists an emeritus recall for April 1–June 30, 2027, which had not begun at the cutoff.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Coauthored preprint updated
strings.timeline.t2.text: The extensive-form equilibrium-selection paper with Srihari Govindan reaches version two; journal acceptance is not established.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Shares the economic sciences prize
strings.timeline.t3.text: Honored with Paul Milgrom for contributions to auction theory and new auction formats.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Named AEA Distinguished Fellow
strings.timeline.t4.text: The American Economic Association recognizes his research on pricing, sequential equilibrium and auctions.
strings.timeline.t5.title: First FCC auction uses simultaneous multiple rounds
strings.timeline.t5.text: The design includes contributions from Wilson, Milgrom, Preston McAfee and others, implemented by the regulator.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Publishes Nonlinear Pricing
strings.timeline.t6.text: Oxford University Press publishes his study of pricing that is not strictly proportional to quantity purchased.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Publishes Sequential Equilibria
strings.timeline.t7.text: The paper with David Kreps appears in Econometrica, advancing analysis of dynamic strategic interaction.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joins Stanford business school
strings.timeline.t8.text: Joins the faculty a year after receiving his Harvard DBA in 1963.
